claims.summary: first_word_after (L89-96) uses split_whitespace() and a trim_matches filter keeping only alphanumeric characters and underscore.
claims.disposition: Verified L89-96 verbatim: split_whitespace, per-chunk trim_matches(|c| !c.is_alphanumeric() && c != '_'), find(!is_empty), to_ascii_lowercase. Exact match.

claims.summary: Snag: a non-alphanumeric/punctuation-heavy follower ([marker] ->, [marker] ...) could make find skip the intended word or return empty, causing the relation check to fail and the marker to be stripped unexpectedly.
claims.disposition: Concern preserved, mechanism contradicted. Source shows the opposite: find(|w| !w.is_empty()) (L93) SKIPS all-punctuation chunks (which trim to empty) to the next real word, so `-> behaves` / `... represents` still isolate the verb and preserve the marker. Stripping happens only when NO alphanumeric word follows (fail-closed). The skip is the robustness, not the bug. Grounded by committed tests L2635, L2884, L2900.
